ssdtMsg1088: Eliminate IRQ conflicts, often used for sound card repairs
ssdtMsg1089:
• HPET (High Precision Event Timer) is a hardware module used for system timing.
• Under macOS, some motherboard HPET devices may cause IRQ (interrupt request) conflicts, which will affect the normal operation of the audio device, causing the system to be unstable or even unable to start.
• This patch adjusts HPET-related ACPI device definitions to avoid IRQ conflicts, ensure that macOS can correctly use HPET timers, fix sound card issues, and improve system stability.
ssdtMsg1090: Counterfeit EC and inject USB power attributes (applicable to Intel 6th generation and above desktop computers)
ssdtMsg1091:
• Applicable to Intel 6th generation and above desktop computers
• This patch will disable the system's original EC device and then create a virtual EC device to "trick" macOS into thinking that a compatible EC exists, thus solving startup problems caused by missing EC devices. 
• Added necessary USB power properties to fix potential issues. Equivalent to merge: SSDT-EC-DESKTOP.aml + SSDT-USBX.aml
ssdtMsg1092: Only counterfeits EC, does not affect existing EC, and injects USB power attributes at the same time (applicable to Intel 6th generation and above notebooks)
ssdtMsg1093:
• Applicable to Intel 6th generation and above notebooks
• Suitable for notebooks, it does not delete or modify the existing EC, but creates a new virtual EC separately to avoid damaging the original EC device and preventing functional abnormalities such as notebook power management and keyboard backlight.
• Added necessary USB power properties to fix potential issues. Equivalent to merging: SSDT-EC-LAPTOP.aml + SSDT-USBX.aml
ssdtMsg1094: Counterfeit EC (applicable to Intel 5th generation and below desktop computers)
ssdtMsg1095:
• Applicable to Intel 5th generation and below desktops
• This patch will disable the system's original EC device and then create a virtual EC device to "trick" macOS into thinking that a compatible EC exists, thus solving startup problems caused by missing EC devices.
ssdtMsg1096: Only counterfeit EC, does not affect existing EC (applicable to Intel 5th generation and below notebooks)
ssdtMsg1097:
• Applicable to Intel 5th generation and below notebooks
• It does not delete or modify the existing EC, but creates a new virtual EC separately to avoid damaging the original EC device and preventing functional abnormalities such as notebook power management and keyboard backlight.
ssdtMsg1098: USB power attribute correction (applicable to Intel 6th generation and newer platforms)
ssdtMsg1099:
• Applicable to Intel Skylake 6th generation and above, server Haswell-E 4th generation and above, AMD Ryzen and other platforms
• Starting with Intel Skylake and newer processors, macOS requires specific USB power properties to ensure that USB devices are properly powered and recognized.
• This patch corrects the power management of USB ports to comply with macOS requirements and solves problems such as abnormal USB device recognition, insufficient power supply, and inability to hot-plug.
• For notebooks: SSDT-EC-LAPTOP.aml + SSDT-USBX.aml The combination of the two is equivalent to SSDT-EC-USBX-LAPTOP.aml
• For desktop: SSDT-EC-DESKTOP.aml + SSDT-USBX.aml The combination of the two is equivalent to SSDT-EC-USBX-DESKTOP.aml
ssdtMsg1100: CPU core identification, enabling frequency adjustment and energy saving correction
ssdtMsg1101:
• SSDT-PLUG is suitable for Intel Haswell 4th generation ~ 11th generation, server Haswell-E 4th generation and above platforms (when customizing SSDT-PLUG, the tool automatically detects and generates it!)
• SSDT-PLUG-ALT is suitable for Intel Alder Lake 12th generation and above, and AMD Ryzen platform (when customizing SSDT-PLUG, the tool automatically detects and generates it and renames it to SSDT-PLUG-ALT!)
• macOS relies on the CPU power management plug-in (PluginType) to adjust the CPU frequency and improve energy efficiency and battery life.
• This patch will modify the CPU definition so that macOS thinks it is a plugin-type = 1 processor required by Apple devices, thereby correctly loading CPU frequency management and improving performance and power consumption control.
ssdtMsg1102: Enable NVRAM support (usually for Intel native 300 series motherboards)
ssdtMsg1103:
• Applicable to Intel Coffee Lake 8th generation ~ 9th generation platforms
• Native 300 series motherboards (such as Z370, B360) may not use NVRAM correctly under macOS, resulting in some functions (such as iMessage, volume memory, boot parameters, etc.) not being saved.
• This patch enables the motherboard's PMC (Power Management Controller), allowing macOS to use native NVRAM normally without the need for an additional EmuVariableUEFI driver.
ssdtMsg1104: Add PNLF device for backlight support (notebooks and all-in-ones only)
ssdtMsg1105:
• macOS requires a PNLF device (Panel Brightness) to correctly control notebook screen brightness.
• This patch will create a PNLF device in ACPI, allowing macOS to adjust screen brightness and display brightness control options in System Preferences.
• Suitable for notebooks and some all-in-one computers to solve the problem of unavailable brightness adjustment.
• UID = 14, applicable to: Intel 1st generation Arrandale, 2nd generation Sandy Bridge, 3rd generation Ivy Bridge
  Note: Some machines using UID: 14 will encounter limited maximum brightness or other problems. In order to solve these problems, the correct device path of the iGPU (integrated graphics card) must be set, and the IGPU register information may need to be supplemented.
• UID = 15, applicable to: Intel 4th generation Haswell, 5th generation Broadwell
• UID = 16, applicable to: Intel 6th generation Skylake, 7th generation Kaby Lake, some 4th generation Haswell
• UID = 17, suitable for: Custom brightness, usually used for some non-standard devices or Hackintosh settings with special needs
• UID = 18, suitable for: Custom brightness, usually used for some non-standard devices or Hackintosh settings with special needs
• UID = 19, applicable to: Intel 8th generation CoffeeLake and above, below 10th generation, and AMD notebooks
• UID = 99, applies to: Others (requires custom applbkl-name / applbkl-data device properties), may not work at all
ssdtMsg1106: Provides sensor support required for screen backlight adjustment (only applicable to notebooks and all-in-one computers)
ssdtMsg1107:
• Used to simulate and enable Apple's native sensor (Ambient Light Sensor, ALS) function to automatically adjust screen brightness
• If your device really has ALS (such as some high-end notebooks) and there are problems, you can try adding SSDT-ALS0 to correct the automatic brightness adjustment function, otherwise it is not recommended to add
• Applicable to: All-in-one PCs (AIOs) and laptops only
ssdtMsg1108: macOS disguises itself as Windows and unlocks blocked devices (such as I2C touchpads)
ssdtMsg1109:
• _OSI (Operating System Interface) is a method of ACPI that allows the operating system to report which features it supports.
• Some motherboard firmware may decide whether to enable certain devices based on the _OSI return value, which may not be recognized by macOS, resulting in loss of functionality.
• The patch "tricks" the firmware into thinking macOS is also Windows, activating hidden features such as: I2C touchpad, battery management, etc.
ssdtMsg1111:
• Some OEMs violate the ACPI specification, which causes problems when booting macOS. To resolve this issue, the RHUB device needs to be shut down and force macOS to rebuild the port manually.
• This patch resets the USB controller (including EHC1, EHC2 and other USB device shielding and renaming) when macOS starts, so that all USB ports can be correctly identified, and is used with USB mapping (such as: UTBMap.kext) to ensure that USB devices work properly.
• Usually suitable for desktop 400 series motherboards (Asus, etc.) and mobile IceLake platforms (Dell, Lenovo, etc.).
ssdtMsg1112: Create bridge for missing PCI device path
ssdtMsg1113:
• The PCI device paths of some motherboards or devices may not be recognized correctly under macOS, causing the device to not work properly, such as graphics cards, sound cards, wireless network cards, etc.
• This patch will create the correct PCI bridges for these devices, ensuring that macOS can correctly recognize and use these PCI devices.
ssdtMsg1114: Remove DMAR reserved memory area, fix system startup problems and network card compatibility issues
ssdtMsg1115:
• DMAR (DMA Remapping Table) is part of Intel VT-d virtualization technology for IOMMU (Input-Output Memory Management Unit) support.
• This patch will remove the reserved memory area in the DMAR table that is causing the problem, thus preventing macOS from misreading the DMAR and causing the system to fail to boot.
• Provide support for VT-d compatibility so that VT-d works properly in macOS Big Sur and newer, especially involving hardware driven by DriverKit.
• macOS supports VT-d, but there are compatibility issues with the DMAR table provided by some motherboards or BIOS, which may cause macOS to cause kernel crashes, startup lags, system instability and other issues when parsing the ACPI DMAR table (stuck in AppleACPICPU, IOPCI, AppleVTD related log locations).
• Supported hardware range: I225 network card, Aquantia network card, some WiFi devices, etc.
• The original DMAR table needs to be dropped in the firmware before the patched table can be loaded.
• Applicable CPU: Any processor that supports VT-d technology.
ssdtMsg1116: Correct the APIC table to solve the CPU kernel panic problem (applicable to HEDT server platform)
ssdtMsg1117:
• Repair or rewrite the Processor ID in the APIC table to ensure that macOS can correctly identify the number and number of CPU cores and avoid kernel panic or core identification errors.
• The original APIC table needs to be dropped in the firmware before the patched table can be loaded.
• Applicable to X58, X79, X99, X299 and other Intel server (HEDT) platforms.
ssdtMsg1119:
• macOS requires an SMBus (System Management Bus) device to properly run certain services, such as:
  I2C touchpad, battery management, light-sensing automatic brightness adjustment, some Wi-Fi/Bluetooth devices
• SSDT-SBUS-MCHC makes macOS think this is a native Apple device by adding SBUS (system management bus) and MCHC (memory controller) devices to ACPI, ensuring that related functions work properly.
• If the device I2C touchpad, battery information, and automatic brightness adjustment cannot be used, you can try to enable this patch.
ssdtMsg1120: Fix the problem of core graphics acceleration failure (usually applicable to Ivy Bridge and Sandy Bridge)
ssdtMsg1121:
• Intel Management Engine (IMEI for short) is a hardware interface used to connect to the management engine. It is only needed when old platforms (Sandy/Ivy) and some motherboards lack MEI/IMEI/HECI devices.
• Applicable to Intel 3rd generation Ivy Bridge processor and 6 series motherboard when mixed (for example: i3 3225 processor, H61 motherboard), core graphics acceleration problem
• Applicable to Intel 2nd generation Sandy Bridge processor and 7 series motherboard when mixed (for example: i5 2500k processor, B75 motherboard), core graphics acceleration problem
• Intel 3rd generation Ivy Bridge processors paired with 7 series motherboards, and Intel 2nd generation Sandy Bridge processors paired with 6 series motherboards do not require this SSDT!
• Intel 4th generation Haswell and newer platforms can usually implement MEI/IMEI/HECI devices correctly and do not need this SSDT!
ssdtMsg1122: Fix the problem of shutting down and restarting or shutting down without power supply
ssdtMsg1123:
• Fixed the problem that some motherboards sometimes do not completely turn off the power to the USB controller when macOS is shutting down (S5), resulting in failure to shut down normally (shutdown becomes restarting or shutdown without power)
• Requires ACPI rename patch: _PTS -> ZPTS
ssdtMsg1124: Check the current system status, mainly to check whether S3 sleep is supported (non-customized SSDT)
ssdtMsg1125:
• Check whether the current machine is an AOAC machine (non-customized SSDT)
• Check the system status in the current BIOS settings, mainly to check whether S3 sleep is supported (non-customized SSDT)
• Note: Only non-AOAC machines are compatible with S3 sleep. AOAC machines conflict with S3 sleep and do not support S3 sleep!
• If the check result shows that the system status of a non-AOAC machine (AOAC machine does not support S3 sleep, do not read below) does not support S3 sleep, there may be the following situations:
  1. The motherboard firmware supports S3 sleep, but S3 sleep is not enabled in the BIOS settings. After it is enabled, S3 sleep can be supported.
  2. The motherboard firmware does not physically castrate S3, but the DSDT does not define the _S3 method. Completing the _S3 method has a probability of fixing the S3 sleep problem.
  3. The motherboard firmware physically castrates S3 and does not support S3 sleep at all. Even if the _S3 method is completed, the S3 sleep problem cannot be repaired.
ssdtMsg1126: Check whether it is an AOAC machine (non-customized SSDT)
ssdtMsg1127:
• Check whether it is an AOAC machine (non-customized SSDT) based on FACP.aml
• Note: Only non-AOAC machines are compatible with S3 sleep. AOAC machines conflict with S3 sleep and do not support S3 sleep! AOAC machines are common in notebooks.
• Once the AOAC machine enters S3 sleep, it may appear that it cannot be woken up after sleeping and appears in a crash state, and can only be forced to shut down. It is recommended to disable S3 sleep.
• AOAC machines recommend considering the following solutions:
  1. Unlock BIOS and disable AOAC (usually difficult to do, but the most stable)
  2. Disable S3 sleep (disable S3 sleep in BIOS, or SSDT-S3-DISABLE to disable S3 sleep)
  3. Turn off the independent graphics power supply
  4. Use NVMeFix.kext to enable APST of SSD
  5. Enable ASPM (BIOS advanced options enable ASPM, SSDT patch enables L1)
ssdtMsg1128: Fix the problem of waking up from sleep due to USB controller
ssdtMsg1129:
• Rename GPRW to XPRW to fix the instant wake-up problem (note: it may cause the USB keyboard to be unable to wake up the device, you can wake it up through the power key)
• SSDT-GPRW is more commonly used because most platforms use the GPRW method and very few platforms provide and use the UPRW method.
• Available for Skylake and newer platforms
ssdtMsg1130: Fix the problem of waking up from sleep due to USB controller
ssdtMsg1131:
• Rename GPRW to XPRW to fix the instant wake-up problem (note: it may cause the USB keyboard to be unable to wake up the device, you can wake it up through the power key)
• SSDT-UPRW is rarely used because most platforms use the GPRW method and very few platforms provide and use the UPRW method.
• Available for Skylake and newer platforms
ssdtMsg1132: Fix sleep button sleep problem (applicable to notebooks)
ssdtMsg1133:
• When some computers enter sleep through the sleep button SLPB (PNP0C0E), ACPI transmits incorrect parameters, causing macOS to mistakenly think it is a shutdown. This may lead to: direct restart, crash after sleep, or successful sleep but damaged system status.
• Pretend "lid is closed" when pressing the sleep button, forcing dangerous PNP0C0E sleep into safe and stable PNP0C0D sleep
• Typically suitable for laptops
ssdtMsg1134: Fixed the issue where you need to press any key to turn on the screen after waking up
ssdtMsg1135: • Fixed the issue where some machines need to press any key to turn on the screen after waking up
ssdtMsg1136: Fix the abnormal breathing light problem of the power button after waking up (applicable to Lenovo notebooks)
ssdtMsg1137:
• Fixed an issue where the breathing light on side A and the breathing light on the power button did not return to normal after waking up on some Lenovo notebooks
• Fixed the issue where the F4 microphone indicator light status is abnormal after waking up on some Lenovo laptops
• Mainly applicable to Lenovo series notebooks, other brands of notebooks are usually not applicable
ssdtMsg1138: Disable system S3 sleep state (fix S3 sleep wake-up crash, restart or shutdown issues)
ssdtMsg1139:
• Only disable S3 sleep state under macOS system to avoid system crash, restart or shutdown when macOS system wakes up
• When disabled, only macOS no longer supports S3 sleep (clicking the sleep button or the monitor enters power-saving mode, the screen turns off, but the host will still run and the fan will not stop running)
• After disabling the S3 sleep state in macOS, you no longer need to modify any system settings of macOS, and you do not need to turn off the energy-saving mode (before this, you may need to modify the system settings -> turn off the display when inactive -> never)
• Applicable scenarios: When the sleep problem has not been repaired, the energy-saving mode is turned on in the macOS system settings ("Turn off the display when inactive -> 10 minutes"). After the system enters sleep state, when the macOS system is awakened, the system may crash, restart or shut down. At this time, the S3 sleep state can be disabled to fix the problem.
• Requires ACPI rename patch: _S3 -> XS3
ssdtMsg1140: Hot restart is changed to cold restart to fix the problem of some hardware being unavailable.
ssdtMsg1141:
• Hot restart is changed to cold restart, which fixes the problem that some hardware becomes unavailable after restarting from Windows to macOS on some platforms. (For example: sound card, WiFi, Bluetooth)
• Note: No SSDT-FACP.aml is generated! Only ACPI-Patch is generated!
ssdtMsg1143:
• Only applicable to AMD graphics cards, SSDT-GPU-SPOOF modifies the device ID read by macOS, making macOS mistakenly think that the graphics card is a supported model, thereby enabling the acceleration function.
• Common graphics card models that need to be counterfeited:
  • AMD Radeon RX 550 Lexa Core
  • AMD Radeon RX 6650XT, RX 6950XT, etc.
ssdtMsg1144: Shield PCI devices, including unsupported graphics cards, NVMe solid-state drives, etc.
ssdtMsg1145:
• There are 3 common methods (OFF, PS3, and IOName can all be blocked) to block unsupported PCIe devices, including unsupported graphics cards, NVMe solid-state drives, wireless network cards, etc. Method priority: OFF > PS3 > IOName
• SSDT-GPU-DISABLE-OFF (applicable to notebooks, desktops generally do not provide an OFF method) by disabling the independent graphics card at the ACPI level, the macOS system can completely not detect the independent graphics card, and the independent graphics card is in a power-off state, thereby saving power consumption and reducing temperature.
• SSDT-GPU-DISABLE-PS3 (applicable to notebooks, desktops generally do not provide the PS3 method) By disabling the independent graphics card at the ACPI level, the independent graphics of the macOS system can stop power supply in the S3 sleep state, thereby saving power consumption and reducing temperature.
• SSDT-GPU-DISABLE-IOName (applicable to all platforms) Modify the graphics card device ID. The macOS system will still detect the graphics card, but the corresponding graphics card driver will not be loaded. The graphics card is in an undriven state, so there is a certain power consumption.
• When the original ACPI table of the notebook does not contain the OFF and PS3 methods, the corresponding SSDT-GPU-DISABLE-OFF and SSDT-GPU-DISABLE-PS3 method shielding will fail. It is recommended to do the next best thing and use the IOName method to shield the PCI device.
ssdtMsg1146: Counterfeit wired network card equipment (applicable to notebooks without wired network cards)
ssdtMsg1147: • Provides NullEthernet fake virtual network card for Hackintosh systems to solve the dependence of iMessage, Facetime, iCloud and other Apple services on built-in network equipment
ssdtMsg1148: Fix notebook I2C touchpad problem (applicable to notebooks)
ssdtMsg1149:
• By repairing the ACPI hardware node mounting, ensuring that the device is enabled in the macOS system, and fixing the problem that some I2C touchpads cannot be recognized normally.
• SSDT-GPI0 solves the problem of driver mounting hardware devices. SSDT-XOSI is mainly used to fix the problem of incompatibility between BIOS/ACPI initialization logic and operating system recognition (sometimes it can fix the touchpad problem)
ssdtMsg1150: CPU renaming for B850, B650, B550, A520 chipsets (only for Ryzen platforms)
ssdtMsg1151:
• Applicable to CPU renaming of B850, B650, B550, and A520 chipsets to fix the crash problem caused by the AMD platform not being able to recognize the CPU (recommended only when using pre-made SSDT patches)
• When customizing the SSDT patch, it is recommended to use the customized SSDT-PLUG! (AMD Ryzen platform automatically changes its name to SSDT-PLUG-ALT when customizing the SSDT)
ssdtMsg1152: Fix power management (applicable to Intel 12th generation and above, some AMD Ryzen and other platforms)
ssdtMsg1153:
• macOS relies on the CPU power management plug-in (PluginType) to adjust the CPU frequency and improve energy efficiency and battery life.
• This patch will modify the CPU definition so that macOS thinks it is a plugin-type = 1 processor required by Apple devices, thereby correctly loading CPU frequency management and improving performance and power consumption control.
• Applicable to Intel Alder Lake 12th generation and above, and some AMD Ryzen platforms
ssdtMsg1154: Disable AWAC (Modern Timer) (available for Intel Coffee Lake 8th generation and above)
ssdtMsg1155:
• Disable AWAC (Modern Timer) while enabling or spoofing legacy RTC
• Compatible with Intel Coffee Lake 8th generation and above
ssdtMsg1156: Required by all native X99 (C612) motherboards and most native X79 (C602) motherboards
ssdtMsg1157:
• This SSDT is applicable to all X99 motherboards and most X79 motherboards. Its main function is to disable unused devices in ACPI to prevent IOPCIFamily from causing kernel panic.
• Applicable motherboards: All native X99 (C612) motherboards and most native X79 (C602) motherboards.
ssdtMsg1158: Enable or fake legacy RTC timer, and fix RTC range (applies to all native X99 (C612) and X299 motherboards)
ssdtMsg1159:
• Enable or fake legacy RTC timers and fix RTC range.
• Solve incorrect boot time, RTC related errors, sleep wake-up issues, etc.
• This SSDT is applicable to all X99(C612) motherboards as well as X299 motherboards
ssdtMsg1161: • Inject hardware device attributes to fix some ACPI issues with graphics cards, sound cards, thunderbolt cards, etc. (When there is no DTGP method support, these attribute injections may fail or not work!)
ssdtMsg1163:

• There is no PNP0C0C in some BIOS/motherboard ACPI trees, and macOS cannot handle the power button correctly, which may result in the inability to sleep, the inability to wake up, and the unavailability of the menu bar power button.
• Add missing parts, this is just a perfect solution, not necessary!
ssdtMsg1167:

• There is no PNP0C0E in some BIOS/motherboard ACPI trees, and macOS cannot handle the sleep button correctly, which may result in the inability to sleep, the inability to wake up, and the unavailability of the sleep button in the menu bar.
